hook_text: Your grandmother leaves you an orchard and a box of gold coins. Which one lasts forever?
clip_script: Two gifts. An orchard that gives fruit every year, as long as you look after the trees. And a box of gold coins: every coin you spend is gone. The orchard is a renewable resource: water, soil, fish, forests, sun and wind. The coins are non-renewable: coal, oil, gold, platinum. Sustainable development means living off the fruit without cutting down the trees, and spending the coins wisely so your children are not left with nothing. Every sector can do it. Farms use drip irrigation and rotate crops. Fishing boats stick to quotas, or you end up like perlemoen, nearly wiped out by poaching. Mines must fix the land when they close. Factories put solar panels on the roof. Shops cut plastic. And the rule is reduce, then reuse, then recycle, because the best rubbish is the rubbish you never made. Bonus: looking after the planet is now a career. Green jobs are growing.
visual_style: An illustrated orchard and a chest of coins side by side, then quick scenes of drip irrigation, a fishing quota sign, a rehabilitated mine, a solar-roofed factory and a shopper with a reusable bag.
pacing: A slow parable opening, a brisk tour of the sectors, an upbeat career close.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and match five careers to the sector that needs them.
